candidates.title: The Milk House: Between the parlor and the pencil
candidates.summary: Soon, I’ll get to take advantage of another honor: attending the World Dairy Expo in the Progressive Dairy booth. Not living in the U.S. now, I haven’t had as many opportunities as I would like to hold readings and speaking events, or to find other opportunities to talk with readers on the ground. However, Progressive Dairy has offered me the chance to sign books and meet with people at their stand.

candidates.title: Capture more of your calves’ true value
candidates.summary: Preconditioning programs, strategic marketing, and postweaning growth can boost returns. Retained ownership reveals true genetic potential.

candidates.title: USDA 2026 milk production forecast shows slight growth
candidates.summary: USDA’s September WASDE report raised 2026 milk production slightly to 237.2 billion pounds on expectations of a larger cow herd and a increase in milk output per cow.

candidates.title: Nepal floods damage 1,800 hectares of crops and kill thousands of livestock
candidates.summary: In this interview, Beth Bechdol, FAO Deputy Director-General, outlines the impact of the floods on rural communities and the urgent path towards agricultural recovery

candidates.title: Cattle futures climb amid corn ease
candidates.summary: October live cattle settled up $1.225 while feeders jumped on weaker corn. Cash remained steady at $218-$223 per hundredweight across regions.

candidates.title: Understanding ionophores
candidates.summary: This class of feed additive is a consumer-safe tool used to improve efficiency, enhance weight gain and prevent cattle diseases.

candidates.title: Last but certainly not least: Tom and Sandy Morris to manage their final World Classic Sale
candidates.summary: For the past 38 years, Tom and Sandy Morris have managed the World Classic Sale at World Dairy Expo. Over the years, they have seen changes, built friendships and made memories, but this year will be their last heading up the sale.

candidates.title: FAO conducted simulation exercises on animal health emergencies in Trinidad and Tobago
candidates.summary: As part of the region's preparedness efforts and actions for potential animal health emergencies, 100 professionals were trained through simulation of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks, with the aim of identifying strengths and possible gaps for improvement in the response.

candidates.title: Beyond first service: The metric that separates repro programs
candidates.summary: Two dairies start their breeding programs looking almost identical. The difference often shows up after the first breeding: One farm quickly identifies open cows returning to heat and breeds them again, while the other waits for a pregnancy check and resynchronization.
